scope.summary: W4 fixture teardown now waits a bounded window for the exact run-owned Oracle sessions to disappear and, if any remain, issues ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION only for sessions re-confirmed to belong to that same exact run, before DROP USER. A call-timeout's asynchronously-reaped server session can no longer cause ORA-01940 or leak fixture users, and no non-run-owned session is ever targeted.
out_of_scope: The call-timeout case itself (scripts/e2e/w4/driver.py, unchanged): this is a teardown fix, not a case fix.
The W4 driver/serve paths and any crates/** source.
The registry binding, ownership sentinel, DROP-target selection, and janitor prefix-discovery rules (all preserved unchanged).
xe18, xe21, and ADB lanes; the live proof is on the loopback free23 lab lane only.

entry_points.name: fixture teardown CLI: python3 scripts/e2e/w4/fixture.py teardown --lane free23 --run-id <id>
entry_points.trace: tests/artifacts/evidence/live/oraclemcp-b0b24-session-reap.json records connected_user_bounded_teardown: a live exact-run owner session is present, teardown_one emits kill_session for that exact run and then drop_user, verdict PASS, elapsed 10.643s within the 45s bound; a foreign run's session survives.

entry_points.name: W4 driver teardown path: scripts/e2e/w4/driver.py finally -> fixture.teardown -> teardown_one
entry_points.trace: teardown_one is the single DROP USER path the driver invokes (driver.py ~line 1891); the bounded reap runs before every DROP USER it issues, so the observed immediate-post-case teardown is covered by the same code path.

limitations: The call-timeout case is exercised by driver.py, not by the fixture selftest; the selftest creates the lingering session directly as the exact run-owned owner user, which is a strictly stronger connected-user condition than an async-reaped timeout.

Oracle offers no conditional kill, so a theoretical SID-reuse race remains between the pre-kill re-check of USERNAME by SID+SERIAL# and the ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION; exact-name filtering bounds the blast radius to this run's schemas.
Proven on free23 only; xe18/xe21/ADB teardown timing is not exercised.
Teardown is bounded, not guaranteed: if a run session survives both windows the run is reported FAIL with sessions_remaining populated rather than waiting indefinitely.
